description: Stable logical identity and memory contract of each DSP. Tools resolve a core by its device-tree unit address, never by remoteprocN. Every region a DSP can address is listed with its owner, whether remoteproc can load ELF segments into it, how much of it the runtime reserves as cache, and the reason for each limit. Linker command files, the C core table, and the ELF validators are generated from or checked against this file (Task 041); section placement itself stays in the editable linker files.
evidence: release/evidence/task-012/20261019T094327Z/dt-memory.json is the live device tree's memory (Task 012); ci/dt_memory.py checks every core here against it and manifest/memory-map.json. The firmware regions follow TI's PDK memory_map_defines.inc, which swaps the two C66x IPC pools on purpose; the device tree assigns them the same way.

cores.name: c66x_0
cores.label: C66x_0

regions.name: dma_pool
regions.reason: Linux allocates this core's vrings and RPMsg buffers here when it starts the core (shared-dma-pool in the device tree, first memory-region of the remoteproc node); TI swaps the two C66x pools on purpose. Firmware must not place anything here.
regions.source: release/evidence/task-008/20261018T175900Z-dmesg.txt; TI PDK 11.02.01.08 ti/drv/ipc/examples/common/j721e/freertos/memory_map_defines.inc and the per-core linker files

regions.name: ddr
regions.reason: Reserved for this core by the device tree (second memory-region of the remoteproc node). The split into resource table, text, data, and heap is a default in the linker files, not a constraint.
regions.source: release/evidence/task-008/20261018T175900Z-dmesg.txt; TI PDK 11.02.01.08 ti/drv/ipc/examples/common/j721e/freertos/memory_map_defines.inc and the per-core linker files

regions.name: l2sram
regions.reason: C66x CorePac L2: 288 KiB at local address 0x00800000. TI's FreeRTOS port configures the top 64 KiB as L2 cache (ti/kernel/freertos/config/j721e/c66/FreeRTOSConfig.h, portCONFIGURE_CACHE_L2_SIZE = 64K, compiled into TI's prebuilt kernel library); the bare-metal runtime leaves L2 at its reset state, all SRAM. remoteproc (k3-dsp-rproc) loads segments addressed at the local L2 view.

regions.name: l1dsram
regions.reason: C66x L1D: 32 KiB at 0x00F00000, configured entirely as cache by both runtimes (FreeRTOS: portCONFIGURE_CACHE_LID_SIZE = 32K; bare metal: reset default). Using it as SRAM requires changing that configuration first.

regions.name: l1psram
regions.reason: C66x L1P: 32 KiB at 0x00E00000, configured entirely as cache by both runtimes (FreeRTOS: portCONFIGURE_CACHE_LIP_SIZE = 32K; bare metal: reset default).

regions.name: msmc
regions.reason: MSMC SRAM, shared by the A72, R5F, and DSP cores. 0x70000000-0x7001FFFF holds ARM Trusted Firmware and 0x707F0000-0x707FFFFF the DMSC firmware, both excluded here. The live device tree (Task 012) shows Linux's mmio-sram driver bound to it with no consumer, so no core owns it. remoteproc cannot load into it. Every DSP's protection denies it (docs/safety.md) until a partition gives each core its own slice; until then firmware must not use it.

regions.name: shared_ddr
regions.reason: DDR reserved by the device tree as memory@aa000000 (28 MiB) for inter-RTOS IPC. The device-manager firmware on MCU R5F core 0 uses it at run time (see manifest/memory-map.json): a DSP that writes here can exhaust that firmware's IPC heap and stop TI-SCI device management for the whole SoC. remoteproc cannot load into it, and every DSP's protection denies it (docs/safety.md).

cores.boot_alignment_reason: The K3 DSP remoteproc driver writes the ELF entry point into the core's boot vector register, which takes a 1 KiB-aligned address on the C66x; it refuses to start firmware whose entry point is not aligned.

mmio_windows.reason: CorePac-local space and SoC configuration below 256 MiB: L2 and L1 memory, the interrupt controller, cache, XMC, and RAT registers, this subsystem's interrupt router (0x00AC0000 or 0x00AD0000), and the DM timer the FreeRTOS tick uses (0x02400000 or 0x02410000).
mmio_windows.source: TI PDK 11.02.01.08 csl/soc/j721e/src/cslr_soc.h, cslr_soc_c66_baseaddress.h, osal/soc/j721e/osal_soc.h (OSAL_FREERTOS_OS_TIMER_ID_C66X_*)

mmio_windows.reason: This subsystem's interrupt router as Sciclient maps it through the C66x RAT (0x00AC0000 plus the RAT region base 0x20000000).
mmio_windows.source: TI PDK 11.02.01.08 drv/sciclient/src/sciclient/sciclient.c (Sciclient_C66xRatMap)

mmio_windows.reason: MAIN NAVSS secure proxy configuration (256 bytes; one 4 KiB MPAX page), which Sciclient uses to reach the system firmware. The MCU NAVSS proxy (0x285B0000, 0x2A380000) is used only by MCU R5F builds; granting it instead made Sciclient_init fail on the board (Task 021, 2026-10-19).
mmio_windows.source: TI PDK 11.02.01.08 drv/sciclient/soc/V1/sciclient_secureProxyCfg.c (the #else branch, which every DSP build takes: CSL_NAVSS0_SEC_PROXY0_*), csl/soc/j721e/src/cslr_soc_baseaddress.h; the C71x ELF's gSciclient_secProxyCfg holds these four addresses

mmio_windows.source: TI PDK 11.02.01.08 drv/ipc/soc/V1/ipc_soc.c, csl/src/ip/navss/V1/cslr_navss_main.h

regions.name: l2sram
regions.reason: C71x L2 SRAM as TI's C7x linker files declare it (448 KiB at 0x64800000); TI's C7x startup configures the remaining L2 as cache. Task 012 confirms the size against the live device tree. Not loadable: the J721E C71x has no local reset, so the kernel loads the ELF while the module is held in reset, and an A72 write into L2 then gets no response and hangs the SoC (a course firmware with a 4-byte .sdos.coeffs and a zero-filled .sdos.runtime in L2 hung the board on 2026-10-19, Task 021). Firmware puts only NOLOAD data and start-up copies (table(BINIT)) here.
regions.source: TI PDK 11.02.01.08 linker_c7x_c7x_1_freertos.lds (L2SRAM 0x64800000, 0x70000); Linux drivers/remoteproc/ti_k3_dsp_remoteproc.c (no local reset for the J721E C71x); release/evidence/task-021

fields.loadable: remoteproc can copy an ELF segment here: the region is in this core's device-tree memory-region list or is the core's own internal memory.
fields.runtime_use: any: code and data; none: firmware must not use it (the reason says why); audit: usable only after Task 012 confirms nothing else owns it, and then only at run time (NOLOAD or copied in).
fields.cache_reserve: bytes at the top of a local SRAM that the runtime configures as cache; firmware may not place anything there under that runtime.
fields.boot_alignment: Required alignment of the ELF entry point, with the loader's reason.
fields.mmio_windows: Address windows outside the core's own memory that its drivers need, mapped read-write and never executable: by the MPAX on the C66x, by the MMU on the C71x. Every other address outside the core's own memory is denied (docs/safety.md). Derived from the PDK sources the firmware links; Task 042's board session confirms them.
